unit.title: Shape and space: properties, 3-D views and angles

objectives.text: Draw 2-D shapes and demonstrate an understanding of line symmetry and knowledge of the relative size of angles.
Interpret plans, elevations and nets of simple 3-D shapes.
Measure angles in degrees and use angles when describing position and direction.

lesson.title: Shape Properties, 3-D Views and Angles
lesson.summary: Use symmetry and angle language to describe shapes, distinguish different two-dimensional views of an object, and give clear directions using degrees.

objectives.text: Draw 2-D shapes and demonstrate an understanding of line symmetry and knowledge of the relative size of angles.
Interpret plans, elevations and nets of simple 3-D shapes.
Measure angles in degrees and use angles when describing position and direction.

sections.heading: Describing 2-D shape properties
sections.body: A line of symmetry divides a shape into matching mirror-image halves. A square has four lines of symmetry, while a non-square rectangle has two. Compare angle sizes by using familiar benchmarks: a right angle is 90 degrees, an acute angle is smaller, and an obtuse angle is larger. Use these properties when checking or drawing shapes.

sections.heading: Understanding views of a 3-D object
sections.body: Plans, elevations and nets are different ways to show a three-dimensional object. A plan is a view from above, while an elevation is a view from one side. A net is a flat arrangement of faces that can fold into a solid. Read the stated view carefully, because it may show length and width but not height.

sections.heading: Using degrees for direction
sections.body: Angles can describe turns and directions as well as shape corners. A quarter turn is 90 degrees, a half turn is 180 degrees, and a full turn is 360 degrees. State whether the turn is clockwise or anticlockwise. Combining a starting direction with an angle gives an unambiguous instruction, such as turn 90 degrees clockwise from north.

practice.prompt: Which statement about a square is correct?
options: It has one line of symmetry.
It has two lines of symmetry.
It has four lines of symmetry.
It has no lines of symmetry.
practice.explanation: A square has four lines of symmetry: vertical, horizontal and two diagonals.

practice.prompt: A plan of a rectangular storage box is viewed from above. Which pair of measurements can that plan show directly?
practice.explanation: A plan is viewed from above, so it can show length and width but not the box's height.

practice.prompt: A person faces north and turns 90 degrees clockwise. Which direction do they face?
practice.explanation: A 90-degree clockwise turn from north is a quarter turn to east.
